name: Helsinki
title: Ship Thickness Measurement Helsinki | Ro-Pax & Ice Class
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Helsinki for ro-pax, ice-class and cargo ships: ice-belt hull structure gauging, pre-docking and scrubber piping.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement and Hull Gauging in Helsinki
intro: Helsinki's ships work a short summer and a long winter. Ro-pax shuttles to Tallinn and overnight ferries to Stockholm run tight timetables, while cargo ships at Vuosaari arrive with ice-scoured hulls after months in the Gulf of Finland. When a superintendent needs ice-belt plating, vehicle decks or ballast tanks gauged before a docking or class survey, we mobilise a team to Helsinki from India, planned around the ship's schedule and the Schengen visa lead time.

highlights.p: Ice abrasion strips coating along the waterline and bow of ice-class hulls. We gauge ice-belt plating and frames so that wastage and ice damage are measured before the spring docking rather than discovered in it.

highlights.h: Vehicle decks and drains on ro-pax
highlights.p: Trucks carry road de-icing salt onto Helsinki's ferries all winter. Vehicle-deck plating, scuppers and drain lines suffer for it, and we measure them during lay-by hours or short service breaks.

Container, ro-ro and Germany-route ro-pax ships at Vuosaari Harbour often stay long enough for deck, hatch-cover and accessible tank gauging, which lets owners firm up a steel list ahead of a Baltic or North Sea docking.

port.h: Helsinki's harbours and the ships that use them
p: The Port of Helsinki is split between passenger harbours in the city centre and a cargo harbour on the eastern edge of the city. West Harbour and Katajanokka carry most of the ro-pax shuttle traffic to Tallinn, one of Europe's busiest passenger crossings, while South Harbour and Katajanokka host the overnight ferries to Stockholm via the Åland Islands. Vuosaari Harbour handles container feeders, ro-ro ships and the ro-pax services to Germany. In summer, cruise ships add to the mix at Hernesaari and the central quays, and the city's own shipyard at Hietalahti builds icebreakers and ice-going special vessels.

Port stays vary sharply by ship type, and that decides how gauging is planned. A Tallinn shuttle is alongside only briefly between crossings and gets its longer breaks at night or during its planned docking. The Stockholm ferries arrive in the morning and sail in the evening, leaving a working day alongside. Cargo ships at Vuosaari are alongside for as long as their cargo work lasts, and in winter ships waiting for a berth or an icebreaker escort lie at the anchorages off the city. Through the summer, Finland's state icebreakers rest at their Katajanokka berth, which is when their maintenance and dockings are scheduled.

What sets Helsinki apart is the combination of ice and intensity of service. Many ships trading here hold a Finnish-Swedish ice class, and every winter in the Gulf of Finland grinds coating off the ice belt and the bow, leaving bare steel to corrode once the ice has gone. Ro-pax ferries add wear of their own: constant berthing, heavy axle loads and salt-laden slush dripping from vehicles attack vehicle decks, scuppers and drain piping. A typical Helsinki UTM scope therefore centres on ice-belt plating and frames, vehicle-deck plating and the drainage system, with ballast tanks and void spaces measured to build up the renewal-survey record over successive visits.

facilities.h: Where gauging is done in and around Helsinki
p: Most gauging in Helsinki happens alongside. On the passenger harbours, work is fitted into the hours when vehicle decks are empty and tanks have been ventilated and certified safe by the ship's crew. At Vuosaari, deck and hold work runs in parallel with cargo operations, with the terminal's safety rules and the stevedores' plan setting the order. Ships at anchor are reached by launch, which in winter depends on ice and weather on the day. For ferries, the useful unit of work is one lay-by: we size each visit so that a complete deck, tank group or drainage section is closed off before the ship sails, rather than leaving half-measured areas to be picked up later.

Dry-docking is a different matter. The yard at Hietalahti concentrates on icebreakers and other ice-going newbuildings, and many ferries and cargo ships trading from Helsinki are docked at repair yards elsewhere around the Baltic. Gauging in Helsinki before the ship leaves gives that yard a measured steel list instead of an allowance, and lets the owner compare yard offers on the same basis. Ultrasonic thickness gauging in Finland before the ship sails also means the surveyor at the yard starts from known figures.
list: West Harbour and Katajanokka — Tallinn and Stockholm ro-pax, gauged in stages during night lay-bys or scheduled service breaks
South Harbour — overnight Stockholm ferries with a working day alongside; vehicle decks, ballast tanks and voids gauged between arrival and departure
Vuosaari Harbour — container, ro-ro and Germany-route ro-pax ships; deck, hatch-cover and accessible tank gauging during cargo operations
Katajanokka icebreaker berths — state icebreakers resting through the summer; hull and ice-belt gauging during their maintenance season
Hietalahti — Helsinki Shipyard's site for ice-going newbuildings; repair and conversion work there can call for UT of welds and crack detection
Anchorages off Helsinki — ships waiting for a berth or ice escort; gauging teams transferred by launch when ice and weather allow

context.h: Ice class, SECA and port state control in Helsinki
p: Finland is a Paris MoU state, and ships calling at Helsinki are targeted for inspection according to their Paris MoU risk profile, so older tonnage with a history of structural deficiencies sees more attention. Since 1 January 2015, fuel used in the Baltic SOx Emission Control Area has been limited to 0.10% sulphur, and Baltic ro-pax and ro-ro operators answered it with a mix of compliant fuel, LNG propulsion and exhaust gas scrubbers. Where scrubbers are fitted, the acidic wash-water and overboard discharge lines become a gauging item in their own right. Voyages between Helsinki and other EU ports are fully inside the EU ETS for shipping, which applies from 2024, and FuelEU Maritime from 2025; both make owners of older ferries think hard about steel renewal against replacement, and the gauging record is the factual basis for that decision.

Ice class is the local constant. The Finnish-Swedish Ice Class Rules set the classes IA Super, IA, IB and IC, and each winter the Finnish authorities publish traffic restrictions that limit which ice classes and sizes may call at each port and receive icebreaker assistance. Keeping a ship's ice class means keeping ice-belt structure within the class requirements, and the ice-class scantling formulas include an addition for abrasion and corrosion that the winter steadily consumes. Ice belt thickness measurement each spring tells the owner how much of that addition is left.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Helsinki
jobs.p: Helsinki work tends to come in two shapes: staged gauging on ships that cannot leave service, and concentrated scopes on ships that stay alongside or are about to dock. In both cases the ice season shapes the timing, because owners want ice-belt figures in hand before the spring docking and before the next winter's traffic restrictions apply. A ship inspection in Helsinki is planned against the ferry timetable or the cargo programme first, then the visa.
list: Ice-belt and bow plating gauging on an ice-class ro-pax at the end of the winter, so the yard can plan renewals before the spring docking
Vehicle-deck plating, scuppers and drain piping on a Tallinn shuttle, gauged across consecutive night lay-bys without taking the ship out of service
Scrubber wash-water and overboard discharge piping on a Germany-route ro-pax at Vuosaari, including the pipe run to the shell penetration accessible from inside
Pre-purchase gauging of an ice-class product tanker or general cargo ship at the anchorage off Helsinki, reported to the buyer's superintendent
Icebreaker hull gauging during the summer maintenance period at the Katajanokka berth, concentrating on the ice belt, bow and stern areas worn by the previous season

logistics: Our team flies into Helsinki-Vantaa Airport and reaches the passenger harbours, Vuosaari or Hietalahti by road. Port access is arranged through the ship's agent: ISPS gate passes for terminal berths, and a launch for ships at anchor. Finland is a Schengen country, and the visa our technicians need has to be applied for well before the job; we fix dates against the ship's docking or lay-by window as early as possible. In winter we also allow for ice and short daylight when planning any external hull work.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a Tallinn shuttle ferry without taking it out of service?
faqs.a: Usually, yes, by splitting the scope. Vehicle decks, voids and accessible tanks can be measured during night lay-bys when the decks are clear, provided the crew has ventilated the tanks and certified them safe for entry. We plan the sequence so each lay-by closes off a complete area. Bottom structure and the full renewal-survey extent of ballast tanks are normally left for the drydock, where staging and cleaning are available.

faqs.q: Do you measure ice-belt plating against the ice-class requirements?
faqs.a: We gauge plating and frames in the ice belt and the forward region and report the readings against the original and minimum thicknesses provided by the ship's drawings or the class society. Judging acceptability is the class surveyor's role. Because ice abrasion concentrates wastage in narrow bands, we use a denser reading pattern along the waterline and at the bow shoulders than a standard hull grid would give.

faqs.q: Is hull gauging in Helsinki practical in mid-winter?
faqs.a: Inside the ship, yes: tanks, holds, decks and piping are measured the same way in January as in June, with low-temperature couplant where spaces are unheated. External shell work is a different story. Alongside or at anchor, ice, cold and short daylight limit what can be reached, so external hull readings are best taken in drydock or planned for the spring.

faqs.q: Can you gauge our ship at Vuosaari during cargo operations?
faqs.a: In most cases. Deck plating, hatch covers and coamings, and void spaces can be measured while cargo is worked, as long as the stevedores' plan and the terminal's safety rules allow access. Holds are measured once they are empty, and tanks once they are gas-free. ISPS passes for the team come through the ship's agent, and we agree the order of work with the chief officer on arrival.
